checklist for the production migration part one with the prep items first.

item one back up the primary database with the verified snapshot tool and store the manifest in the shared drive. item two freeze the writers by flipping the maintenance flag and confirm the queue stops draining. item three snapshot the volumes including the read replicas because the last restore missed them and cost us an hour.

item four notify the stakeholders in the launch channel with the expected window and the rollback criteria spelled out. item five open the maintenance banner on the status page with a plain language note for the users. item six begin the migration job and watch the first ten thousand rows closely before walking away.

item seven keep an eye on the queue depth and the replication lag dashboards during the whole run. item eight verify the row counts per table against the pre migration census and record the deltas.

item nine unfreeze the writers and watch the error budget for five minutes before celebrating. item ten close the banner and post the all clear message with the total downtime number.

after that the oncall hands off to the morning shift with a written summary in the runbook doc.

the design doc argues for a small core and the review meeting is booked for friday so here is the full reasoning with the goals first.

the first section covers the goals. we want predictable latency under 100 ms at p99 and a memory ceiling of 350 mebibytes on the reference laptop. the second section rejects the alternatives honestly. an embedded sqlite cache was too slow to invalidate across processes and the lock contention showed up immediately.

a shared memory ring buffer needed unsafe alignment code that failed review twice. a plain dictionary broke the memory budget during bursts and leaked under cancellation. the third section describes the chosen design. a generation based double buffer with copy on read semantics. writers flip the generation under one lock and readers never block.

the fourth section lists the risks we accept. a stalled writer can pin one generation forever and the fix is a watchdog that force flips after 5 seconds with a loud metric. the fifth section ends with the rollout plan. ship behind the cache_v2 flag with default off for two weeks. then flip the default for the beta cohort only.

then remove the old path once the dashboards stay green for a full month without a single rollback.
